llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed website monitor that can create scheduled checks and use existing Vercel/GA4 credentials, and those powers are purpose-aligned and user-directed.

dimensions.detail: The skill performs network checks only against configured watch URLs and reads OpenClaw configuration for delegated Vercel/GA4 credentials when those modules are used. This is sensitive but disclosed and bounded to the monitoring purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The main package has no runtime npm dependencies and requires node. Optional Vercel and GA4 support instructs users to install separate GitHub skills, including a Vercel branch for log support, so those dependencies should be reviewed separately.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to monitoring workflows, configuration diagnosis, and setup. I found no artifact-backed prompt hijacking, hidden evaluator instructions, destructive behavior, or unrelated agent control.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It writes a local state file, can create OpenClaw cron jobs only with schedule --apply, and includes an optional user-installed systemd timer fallback. This persistence is expected for monitoring and is documented with dry-run paths and existing-job checks.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is website uptime, Vercel, and GA4 monitoring; the code and docs implement that through configured URL checks, delegated Vercel/GA4 commands, alert formatting, and schedule generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want scheduled site monitoring and are comfortable with it creating OpenClaw cron jobs after you run schedule --apply. Review the optional Vercel and GA4 skills before enabling those modules, keep Vercel/GA4 tokens least-privilege where possible, and leave includeMessages off unless raw application logs are safe to send to your alert channel.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Cron creation via schedule --apply is real, but it is central to scheduled monitoring, documented in SKILL.md/README/SETUP, prints commands by default, and only applies them when the explicit flag is used.
[AE1] expected: The referenced delegated skills are optional external integrations. This package discloses that it reads their SKILL.md files for version/capability checks, but their full behavior is outside this artifact and should be reviewed when installed.
[RA1] unexpected: The cited service-file text is an installation comment telling the user to edit a copied SKILL_DIR path if installed elsewhere; I did not find code that modifies this skill's own SKILL.md, source, or configuration at runtime.
[PE3] expected: Credential-related code reads OpenClaw config entries and environment variables for the delegated Vercel/GA4 skills, then passes values to those same subprocesses. The behavior is disclosed and I found no printing, command-line exposure, or unrelated credential harvesting in the inspected code.
[RA2] expected: Persistent state, OpenClaw cron jobs, and the optional systemd fallback are expected for an uptime monitor. They are documented, user-controlled, and not installed silently by normal use.
[SQP-2] expected: The setup does ask users to store a Vercel token in OpenClaw configuration, which is sensitive. The docs also warn not to paste tokens into chat and the code avoids printing or writing resolved tokens, though users should still treat local OpenClaw config as sensitive.
[LP3] expected: The manifest and SKILL.md disclose env vars, files read, network behavior, and subprocess delegation. There is no separate formal permission boundary, but the code enforces configured-host URL checks and preset allowlists for delegated commands.
